title: Félix Díaz's felicista conspiracy: agents' letters with code-name passages the cataloguers left "claves no descifradas"
correspondents: Pablo Ariza ("José Mina"), Pedro Duhart, Arturo A. Amaya, Javier Lozano, Charles Moneglia, Manuel de la Hoz ("Manuel Escudero"), Isauro Suárez and others → Félix Díaz and his aliases (José González, R. W. Greer, Pedro Suárez, Guillermo Rosas Jr.)
shelfmark: CEHM-Carso, Fondo DCXXI (Archivo de Félix Díaz): DCXXI.3.231.1 (Duhart, NY 29 Aug 1921, 21 code names), DCXXI.3.242.1 (Amaya, Havana 27 Sep 1921), DCXXI.3.263.1 and 3.278.1 (Mina, 8 and 30 Nov 1921), DCXXI.3.256.2 (2 Nov 1921, signer in code), DCXXI.3.288.1 (Suárez, 17 Dec 1921), DCXXI.3.301.2, DCXXI.3.323.1 (12 Jan 1922), DCXXI.5.474.2 (Lozano, 10 May 1922), DCXXI.5.514.1 (Moneglia, 10 Jun 1922), DCXXI.6.576.1 (25 Aug 1922), DCXXI.7.656.1 (Escudero, 6 Nov 1921)
folio_note: About 12 typed letters, each with a handful of enciphered names or short runs; CEHM marks them Formato Digital (scans exist, viewing needs a CEHM reader account)
status: CEHM catalogue: "incluye claves no descifradas" / "clave sin descifrar" on each record. Narváez (2015) broke two members of this family (Argumedo's number-pair names, DCXXI.3.244.1 / 3.250.2, and the Wellington letter DCXXI.6.588.1, a "modern method" letter cipher) and showed the catalogue phrase means "cipher not translated"; the other letters listed here are not discussed in his article.
why: Names of the officers, financiers and agents in the 1921-22 felicista plots against Obregón, which the letters hide on purpose.
score_note: Scored from the CEHM online catalogue record during the Oct 2026 Mexico sweep (research/latam_mexico/); not viewed
verify: Read Narváez 2015 sections 2-3 for the two systems; open each record's digital copy at CEHM (reader account) and test the Argumedo pair table and the Wellington method on them.
